candidate_relations.reason: The clinical picture—10-year history, expansile lytic bony lesion involving orbital roof/frontal bone/sphenoid wing on CT, heterogeneous enhancing mass on MRI, no endocrine history—is classic for fibrous dysplasia. Meningioma of the orbital roof is a plausible differential (it can cause proptosis and orbital roof involvement) but represents a different pathological entity (neoplastic meningothelial vs. fibro-osseous dysplastic bone). The CT description of an expansive lytic bony lesion with involvement of multiple bony walls (frontal bone, sphenoid wing) favors fibrous dysplasia over meningioma, which typically causes hyperostosis rather than a purely lytic expansile bony lesion. The candidate asserts an incompatible etiology and tissue type.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Meningioma is a distinct neoplastic entity; fibrous dysplasia is a fibro-osseous developmental lesion of bone

case_quality_flags: Imaging description could support either fibrous dysplasia or meningioma; however, expansile lytic multi-wall bony involvement with 10-year indolent course strongly favors fibrous dysplasia over meningioma
